title: What is known about 1RB0RF_0LC1LB_1RD1LA_1RE0LC_0RA1RD_---0RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_0LC1LB_1RD1LA_1RE0LC_0RA1RD_---0RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Lean proves the word conversions (D and E going right make level-k words dense for k = 1..3 and 1..2, C going left makes level-1 words sparse). The level boundaries and the staircase on the right, where it could halt, were not derived.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Word conversions
claims.text: D> (011(01)3k)n → (001 16k)n D> for k = 1, 2, 3; E> (101(10)3k)n → (100 16k)n E> for k = 1, 2; (1700)n C> 1 → C> 1 (011010101)n; D> (011)n → (001)n D>.

claims.title: Level-2 C conversion
claims.text: (11300)n C> 1 → C> 1 (011(01)6)n in 65n steps, checked by symtm; its Lean proof hits the recursion limit and was left out.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: Only F reading 0 halts; F is entered only from A reading 1 (0RF), so the machine halts exactly on A> 1 0. Read off the table.

claims.title: The tape over time
claims.text: At 4·109: (100)2498 (9-cell)662 (100)3 (15-cell)32 10 A>0 (15-cell)1592 ... (21-cell)95 ... then 39 blocks (111)3 011011(01)7 and further right blocks (111)m 011011(01)j with m growing to 22.

claims.title: Same emergent machine as 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD0RF
claims.text: Different tables, but both build runs of the same (6k+3)-cell words and flip them between dense and sparse form as the head passes, and both end in the same staircase of 13m 011011(01)j blocks. Observed only.

claims.title: No closed tape language with small windows
claims.text: bbtools.ctl K = 3..6 leaves halting configurations; n-gram CPS fails; no invariant mod 2..12.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 30,226 cells have been visited and 19,357 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.517). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.112).

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The machine stops only on A> 1 0; the proved conversions never produce it inside a run, so the question is about the level boundaries and the staircase on the right, whose rules were not derived.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 30,226 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Levels of 9-, 15-, 21-cell words and a staircase
html: At step 4·109, left to right: 2,498 copies of 100, a run of 662 nine-cell words, a run of 15-cell words cut by the head (32 left of it, 1,592 right of it), a run of 95 21-cell words, then a staircase of blocks (111)m 011011(01)j with m growing from 3 to 22 along the tape.
The level-k word has length 6k + 3 and two forms: dense 16k+100 and sparse 011(01)3k. This is the same picture as in 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_1RE0LA_1RA1RD_0RD0RF, though the tables differ.

sections.heading: Going right makes words dense, going left makes them sparse
html: Lean proves that D going right turns sparse words of levels 1 to 3 into dense ones, E does the same for levels 1 and 2 from another rotation, and C going left turns dense level-1 words back into sparse ones (level 2 was checked by the symbolic tool only). So the head is a bouncer that flips words as it passes; the moving boundaries between levels are not derived.

sections.heading: Only on A> 1 0
html: Only F reading 0 stops the machine, and F is reached only from A reading 1 and stepping right, so it stops exactly when A stands on 1 0. That does not happen inside a run; it could happen at a boundary or in the staircase.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.517). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.112).
After 109 steps the tape spans 30,226 cells (22,819 left of the start, 495 right), with a density of 1s of 0.64.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A cousin of 1RB0RF_0LC---_1LD1LC_...: the same multi-level bouncer of (6k+3)-cell words, dense 1^(6k+1) 00 on one side of the head and sparse 011 (01)^(3k) on the other, ending in a staircase of 1^(3m) 011011(01)^j blocks on the right.
